record.original_question: Let M be a closed manifold that is not a K(pi,1), and let Sigma be a closed connected hypersurface in T^*M that is a regular energy level of a Hamiltonian H: T^*M -> R. Is there always some epsilon > 0 such that almost all energy levels of H in the interval (c - epsilon, c + epsilon) carry a contractible periodic orbit of H?

evidence.quote: Problem statementLetMbe a closed manifold that is not aK(π,1), and endow the cotangent bundleT ∗Mwith its standard symplectic form. We conjecture that, for any closed and connected hypersurfaceΣ⊂T ∗Mand any HamiltonianH:T ∗M→Rthat admitsΣas a regular energy levelΣ =H −1(c), there existsε >0such that almost all energy levels ofHin the interval(c−ε, c+ε)carry a contractible periodic orbit ofH.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a closed smooth manifold that is not a $K(\pi,1)$ (i.e., its universal cover is not contractible, equivalently some higher homotopy group $\pi_k(M)$ with $k\ge 2$ is nontrivial). Equip the cotangent bundle $T^*M$ with its standard symplectic form $\omega = d\lambda$, where $\lambda$ is the canonical Liouville $1$-form. Given a smooth Hamiltonian $H : T^*M \to \mathbb{R}$, the Hamiltonian vector field $X_H$ is defined by $\iota_{X_H}\omega = -dH$, and a periodic orbit of $H$ on the energy level $H^{-1}(a)$ is a non-constant solution $\gamma : \mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z} \to T^*M$ of $\dot\gamma = X_H(\gamma)$ lying in $H^{-1}(a)$. Such an orbit is called contractible if its underlying free loop in $T^*M$ is contractible (equivalently, since $T^*M$ deformation retracts to $M$, its projection to $M$ is contractible).

Suppose $\Sigma \subset T^*M$ is a closed connected hypersurface that arises as a regular energy level $\Sigma = H^{-1}(c)$ of some smooth Hamiltonian $H$ (so $dH$ is non-vanishing on $\Sigma$). 

Question: Does there always exist $\varepsilon > 0$ such that for almost every (in the sense of Lebesgue measure) value $a \in (c-\varepsilon, c+\varepsilon)$, the energy level $H^{-1}(a)$ carries a contractible periodic orbit of $H$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as a conjecture concerning contractible almost-existence on hypersurfaces in cotangent bundles of closed manifolds that are not aspherical. Related almost-existence theorems are known (e.g., for non-contractible orbits via Macarini–Schlenk, and contractible orbits in symplectically aspherical or low-energy settings), but a search did not produce a resolution of the contractible almost-existence statement in this specific generality (closed M not a K(π,1), arbitrary closed connected regular hypersurface). The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: An almost existence theorem for non-contractible periodic orbits in cotangent bundles
status_evidence.snippet: Almost every energy level carries a periodic orbit representing a non-trivial free homotopy class.
status_evidence.claim: Related almost-existence results address non-contractible orbits, complementary to the contractible case considered here.

status_evidence.title: Noncontractible periodic orbits in cotangent bundles and Floer homology
status_evidence.snippet: Existence of noncontractible periodic orbits in cotangent bundles via Floer homology.
status_evidence.claim: Existing literature handles noncontractible cases; the contractible-orbit conjecture for non-aspherical base remains a conjecture.
